content: Always recap and confirm customer pain points early to build trust, especially with skeptical buyers.
When a product has a weakness (e.g., keyboard flex on lap), proactively offer a physical accessory or workaround to turn it into a solution.
Avoid making unsubstantiated competitor claims; instead, let the customer experience the difference firsthand.
In a retail setting, use every opportunity for hands-on demonstration to overcome objections.
For proxy buyers (e.g., child buying for parent), address the end-user's concerns directly and provide clear, verifiable answers.

name: Pain Point Recap Trust Builder
condition: When customer has multiple pain points and high skepticism.
example: After initial needs discovery, summarize the customer's pain points and ask for confirmation before proposing solutions.

name: Accessory Solution Turnaround
condition: When a product feature has a known weakness in a specific use case.
example: If the keyboard wobbles on lap, immediately offer a lap desk or rigid surface and let the customer test it.

name: Live Demo Competitor Deflection
condition: When customer mentions a competitor and you have a comparative advantage.
example: Instead of making claims, set up a side-by-side test and let the customer experience the difference.

rebuttal_template: I understand your concern. Let me show you our [accessory name]—it's designed to provide a stable surface. Here, try typing on it yourself. You'll feel the difference immediately.

I respect that. Let's do a quick side-by-side test. Here's our tablet with the keyboard, and here's a Samsung model. Type a few lines on both—you'll notice our magnetic lock keeps it steady even on a soft surface.

objection: Are there hidden costs for the pen features?
rebuttal_template: Absolutely no hidden costs. Let me open the Notes+ app right now and show you: write on this PDF, save it, and share it via email—all without any subscription. You can see it's all included.
